questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of a ‘right’?
options: A) It can be revoked by the government at any time
B) It is a power granted by the people
C) It is a fundamental entitlement guaranteed by law
D) It is a privilege that can be taken away

questions.question: What is the role of opposition parties in a democracy?
options: A) To criticize and hold the government accountable
B) To support the ruling party
C) To control the media
D) To replace the ruling party immediately

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a constitution in a democracy?
options: A) To give more power to the government
B) To regulate the military
C) To limit the rights of citizens
D) To define the structure of government and protect rights

questions.question: Who can contest elections in a democracy?
options: A) Only members of the ruling party
B) Only the rich and powerful
C) Anyone who meets the legal qualifications
D) Only appointed officials

questions.question: What is the role of citizens in a democracy?
options: A) To obey all orders from the government
B) To participate in elections and other democratic processes
C) To remain silent and passive
D) To work for the government only

questions.question: What is the main difference between a democracy and a dictatorship?
options: A) In democracy, people elect their leaders; in dictatorship, leaders are not elected
B) Democracy allows free speech, but dictatorship does not
C) Democracy supports human rights, but dictatorship does not
D) All of the mentioned

questions.question: Who is responsible for enforcing the law in a democracy?
options: A) The military
B) The executive branch of government
C) The judicial system
D) Citizens

questions.question: Which body is responsible for conducting elections in India?
options: A) Election Commission
B) Parliament
C) Judiciary
D) Political parties

questions.question: What does “majority rule” mean in a democracy?
options: A) The minority has all the power
B) Only the wealthy can decide laws
C) The largest group of elected representatives makes decisions
D) The ruler makes all decisions alone

questions.question: Who can become the Prime Minister in India?
options: A) Any citizen
B) Only the wealthy
C) Only the President
D) Any member of Parliament

questions.question: What is the role of the media in a democracy?
options: A) To support only the ruling party
B) To report unbiased news and inform citizens
C) To limit citizens’ access to information
D) To act as a propaganda tool for the government

questions.question: What is a “coalition government”?
options: A) A government formed by multiple parties working together
B) A government controlled by the military
C) A government run by one party
D) A government with no elected representatives

questions.question: What is the “Right to Information” in India?
options: A) The right to only vote in elections
B) The right to start a business
C) The right to receive any public service for free
D) The right to access government records and information

questions.question: What is the function of the Election Commission of India?
options: A) To create political parties
B) To control media outlets
C) To make laws
D) To conduct free and fair elections

questions.question: What is “civil society”?
options: A) The military and police forces
B) The part of society controlled by the government
C) A society with no political rights
D) The part of society that consists of organizations and groups working to promote human rights and democracy

questions.question: Who is responsible for safeguarding the rights of citizens in a democracy?
options: A) The President
B) The Judiciary
C) The Military
D) The Prime Minister

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the ‘Right Against Exploitation’?
options: A) Article 23
B) Article 19
C) Article 17
D) Article 21

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of the electoral system in India?
options: A) Voting is compulsory
B) Only the rich can vote
C) Citizens elect their representatives in free and fair elections
D) It is based on a monarchy

questions.question: What is electoral politics?
options: A) Politics related to economic policies
B) Politics related to the voting process and elections
C) Politics related to the military
D) Politics related to international relations

questions.question: Why are elections held in a democracy?
options: A) To promote dictatorship
B) To ensure that one leader holds all the power
C) To allow citizens to choose their representatives and hold them accountable
D) To reduce the influence of political parties

questions.question: What are democratic rights?
options: A) Rights given only during emergencies
B) Rights granted only to a few citizens
C) Rights that can be revoked at any time
D) Rights that protect individual freedoms and ensure participation in political life

questions.question: Which of the following is a democratic right guaranteed by the Constitution?
options: A) Right to freedom of speech and expression
B) Right to receive a government salary
C) Right to inherit property
D) Right to own a business

questions.question: What does universal adult franchise mean?
options: A) Voting is restricted to government employees
B) Only educated citizens can vote
C) All adults, regardless of their wealth or education, have the right to vote
D) All citizens must vote

questions.question: What is the role of the legislature in a democracy?
options: A) To administer the military
B) To appoint judges
C) To enforce laws
D) To make laws and pass budgets

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the Parliament in India?
options: A) To handle diplomatic relations
B) To make and amend laws, represent the people, and oversee the executive
C) To control the judiciary
D) To enforce laws

questions.question: What was a major feature of the South African Constitution post-apartheid?
options: A) It legalized segregation
B) It gave full power to the military
C) It promoted equality and ended racial segregation
D) It abolished voting rights for all citizens

questions.question: What is the role of a voter’s list?
options: A) To decide who wins the election
B) To set the electoral date
C) To monitor campaign speeches
D) To determine the eligibility of voters

questions.question: What is the process of polling in elections?
options: A) Campaigning for a party
B) Voting to select representatives
C) Counting the votes after elections
D) Announcing election results

questions.question: How is a major policy decision taken in a democracy?
options: A) By the military
B) By one individual leader
C) By elected representatives through discussion and consensus
D) By a non-elected body

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of cultural rights?
options: A) Right to vote
B) Right to own property
C) Right to freedom of religion
D) Right to preserve one’s language and culture

questions.question: What is the purpose of elections in a democracy?
options: A) To limit political participation
B) To choose leaders and representatives
C) To make laws directly
D) To suppress opposition

questions.question: What is the right to equality?
options: A) Everyone must be treated the same by the government
B) Some people are given more privileges
C) Only rich people are equal before the law
D) It restricts the rights of citizens

questions.question: What does the Right to Information (RTI) allow citizens to do?
options: A) To restrict access to government records
B) To seek information from the government
C) To stop government decisions
D) To refuse to participate in elections

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of direct democracy?
options: A) Citizens electing representatives to make decisions for them
B) A monarchy where a king decides on the laws
C) Citizens voting on a specific law or policy directly
D) Citizens having no role in decision-making

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a guiding value of the Indian Constitution?
options: A) Justice
B) Equality
C) Freedom
D) Monarchy

questions.question: What is the purpose of reserved constituencies in India?
options: A) To ensure the ruling party wins
B) To represent specific groups like Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
C) To allow only certain political parties to contest
D) To limit the number of candidates in an election

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the role of the President of India?
options: A) The President leads the government
B) The President makes laws
C) The President is the ceremonial head of state
D) The President controls the military

questions.question: How often are elections held for the Lok Sabha in India?
options: A) Every year
B) Every 3 years
C) Every 10 years
D) Every 5 years

questions.question: In India, what is the age requirement to vote in elections?
options: A) 18 years
B) 21 years
C) 25 years
D) 16 years

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Parliament of India?
options: A) It consists only of the Lok Sabha
B) It is made up of two houses: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
C) It only passes laws related to education
D) It is controlled by the Prime Minister

questions.question: Who drafts the constitution of a country?
options: A) Foreign leaders
B) The military
C) A group of elected representatives
D) The president

questions.question: Who helps the President in running the country?
options: A) The military
B) The judiciary
C) The Parliament
D) The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers

questions.question: What is the Right to Freedom in India?
options: A) The right to do anything without restrictions
B) The right to express opinions, assemble, and move freely
C) The right to be free from all rules
D) The right to only follow one religion

D) Agriculture

options: A) Subsistence farming
B) Extensive farming
C) Modern farming
D) Shifting cultivation

questions.question: What is the most common source of irrigation in Palampur?
options: A) Tube wells
B) Ponds
C) Canals
D) Rainwater

options: A) To increase soil fertility

D) Because they do not have enough land

questions.question: What does ‘capital’ mean in production?

C) Only money used for investment
D) None of the above

questions.question: How does transport help the economy of Palampur?
options: A) It connects the village to markets and cities

D) It increases unemployment
